title: Tenant guardrails: centralized egress policy center and shared-link blocker
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Enterprise customers require finer-grained admin controls to prevent accidental data exfiltration while preserving developer productivity. Current compliance toggles are siloed (IP whitelist + sharing disable + export block) and lack a central place for policy visibility and coordinated enforcement. This ticket implements a centralized 'Egress Policy Center' in the Console paired with a tenant-level 'Shared Link Blocker' toggle and RBAC v2 enforcement surface.

Scope & Goals:
- Add a Console page 'Egress Policy Center' that consolidates: IP allowlists (per-tenant + per-route override), public sharing controls (disable shared links and ephemeral links), and data export controls (CSV/JSON download, S3 export, API bulk export).
- Enforce policy at the request routing layer: policy checks must run before model selection and streaming begins to ensure no partial responses are emitted on denied flows.
- Integrate with RBAC v2 such that only users with admin.policy_manage can change these toggles; audit events must capture who changed what and when.
- Emit structured audit logs (JSON) for toggles and enforcement decisions to the tenant audit sink and default system audit log.
- Provide a migration path from existing per-organization toggles to the new tenant-level policy definitions.

Acceptance criteria:
1) UI: Egress Policy Center page shows current effective policy, live preview of policy resolution (tenant + project + route), and a two-step confirmation for turning on 'block public sharing'.
2) API: New admin API endpoints (/v1/admin/egress-policies) allow read/write of tenant policy JSON. Only users with admin.policy_manage are able to write.
3) Enforcement: Requests blocked by policy return a standardized 403 with a telemetry code and an audited event containing request metadata, resolved policy id, and decision reason.
4) Audit: Toggle changes and enforcement decisions produce audit log entries with fields: actor_email, actor_id, tenant_id, change_set, prev_state, new_state, timestamp, change_origin (console|api|auto-migration).
5) Migration: Existing org toggles are migrated to the tenant policy with a dry-run phase where both old toggles and new policy can be read; an admin can flip 'apply-migration' to complete migration.
6) Tests: Unit and integration tests that cover UI, API permission checks, enforcement at the routing layer, and audit log formatting.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Policy language: we will start with a declarative JSON schema (allowlist, denylist, actions) rather than a full policy DSL to shorten time-to-value. Allows constrained expressivity but simpler verification and predictable enforcement.
- Enforcement point: Doing checks at request router vs model runtime. We choose request router to avoid partial token leakage and to centralize enforcement logic. This imposes additional latency (microseconds) but avoids complex instrumentation in model runtimes.
- RBAC gating: Enforce via RBAC v2 permission check at REST gateway. This means older API tokens may need rotation if they lack the new permission set—documented in migration notes.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Backend: Add EgressPolicyService (API + storage) in control-plane (schema migration for tenant_policy table). Implement permission checks integrated with RBAC v2 library and versioned API endpoints.
2) Router: Add policy-evaluation middleware in the router that resolves effective policy and decides allow/block; emit audit event synchronously to internal audit queue.
3) Console: Build Egress Policy Center UI with preview/resolution visualization, enable/disable toggles, and migration controls.
4) Audit: Extend existing audit pipeline to accept new structured events and wire to tenant sinks.
5) Migration script: Safe migration with dry-run and apply phases; banner in Console during dry-run to warn admins.
6) Tests + E2E: Simulate common enterprise workflows (shared link creation, large export) to validate blocking and logging.

APIs & Contracts (sketch):
- GET /v1/admin/egress-policies?tenant_id=... -> returns effective policy JSON + resolution path
- PUT /v1/admin/egress-policies/{tenant_id} -> write new tenant policy (requires admin.policy_manage)
- POST /v1/admin/egress-policies/{tenant_id}/migrate -> dry-run/apply

Audit event example (stringified record in JSON):
- name: tenant.egress_policy.change
- payload fields (as strings): actor_email, actor_id, tenant_id, change_set (stringified diff), prev_state, new_state, timestamp, change_origin

Rollout & Migration notes:
- Phase 1 (dry-run): Policy center visible, enforcement runs in 'log-only' mode for 7 days for customers with >1TB data egress historically. Events are logged but not enforced.
- Phase 2 (opt-in enforcement): Admins can enable enforcement per tenant.
- Phase 3 (mandatory enforcement): New tenants default to strict policies; existing tenants must opt-in by migration apply or accept default mapping after notification.

Security & Compliance considerations:
- All change APIs require SSO/SAML admin assertion and must be logged.
- RSA-based signing for migration apply events to prevent replay.
- KMS-protected storage for any exported policy artifacts.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should per-route overrides be additive or replace tenant-level lists? (Defaulting to additive today.)
- How to present complex policy resolution in a way that security reviewers trust? (Need UX + legal review.)
- Data residency: where audit events are stored for private deployments? (Consult Private infra team.)

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.company/egress-policy-center-proposal (design spec)
- Figma: https://figma.com/file/egress-policy-center (UI mocks)
- GH: PR #8124 (router middleware) and PR #8150 (admin API), branches: feature/egress-policy-center/*

Notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the tenant-level control plane and router enforcement. Follow-up tickets will cover per-route UX polish, audit retention configuration, and automated remediation playbooks.
